use_case_name: Display and Export System Information Logs

evidence_cards.content: The system shall display information logs and provide the capability to export the logs in common ASCII text for importing to commercial database, spreadsheet, or reporting programs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This statement explicitly defines the high-level objective of the use case: to display and export system information logs.

evidence_cards.content: The system shall generate log files as follows for reports.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This statement defines the high-level objective of the use case: to produce specific log files intended for reporting purposes.

evidence_cards.content: The I-15 Reversible Lane Control System includes an entity named 'Operator Daily Diary Log' (Entity ID 17) which is directly associated with the 'Personnel' entity.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a specific log type ('Operator Daily Diary Log') that corresponds to the use case objective of displaying and exporting system information logs for the Operator.

evidence_cards.content: The Operator is the only user class authorized to have command control of the system during normal mode.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that the Operator must be in 'normal mode' to exercise command control, which is a necessary system state precondition for initiating log display and export functions.

evidence_cards.content: Only one 'operator' may be logged onto the system at any given time.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a concurrency constraint on the Operator role; implies that a valid operator session must exist and be exclusive before the use case can proceed.

evidence_cards.content: The system shall display information logs and provide the capability to export the logs in common ASCII text for importing to commercial database, spreadsheet, or reporting programs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the functional capability that must be available before the Operator can perform the use case actions of displaying and exporting logs.

evidence_cards.content: The Operator Daily Diary Log (Entity 17) is an entity in the system that records operator activities.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a specific log type relevant to the use case 'Display and Export System Information Logs', implying its existence as a potential precondition for display/export operations.

evidence_cards.content: The Device Command Log (Entity 10) is an entity in the system that records device commands.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies another specific log type relevant to the use case, indicating it must exist in the system before it can be displayed or exported.

evidence_cards.content: The System Operation Command Log (Entity 35) is an entity in the system that records system operation commands.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a third specific log type relevant to the use case, indicating it must exist in the system before it can be displayed or exported.

evidence_cards.content: When no operator is logged on to the system, the status of all devices will continue to be monitored and displayed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that device monitoring and display functions are active even in unattended mode (no operator logged in), which is a precondition for any subsequent operator-initiated use case like displaying/exporting logs — implying these capabilities do not require prior login to function at baseline level.

evidence_cards.content: If a scheduled operational sequence requires an operator to be logged on to confirm each step of the operation, an audible alarm will sound to alert the operator to log on to the system.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Indicates that certain operations (including potentially log export/display if part of a scheduled sequence) may require operator login as a precondition — but only if explicitly configured in a scheduled sequence; otherwise, no login is required for basic monitoring/display. This defines a conditional precondition based on operational context.

evidence_cards.content: The following logs are required: Device Command Log, System Operation Command Log, Problem Work Order Log, Alarm Log (Critical and Warning Alarm), Operator Daily Diary Log, Maintenance Log, and System Operation Schedule log.

evidence_cards.content: Not including device and network response times, requests from the GUI for status updates shall not exceed 2 seconds to update the GUI display.

evidence_cards.content: Not including device and network response time, requests from the GUI for device status changes (control commands) shall not exceed 2 seconds.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a performance constraint for control commands, distinguishing them from status updates, which helps define the scope of the 'display' action versus 'control' actions in the use case.

evidence_cards.content: The system shall generate log files as follows for reports: Device Command Log (contains device commands issued with time stamp, operator ID, unit where the command was issued at and shall include failed or aborted commands), System Operation Command Log (contains system operational commands issued with time stamp, operator ID, unit where the command was issued at and shall include failed or aborted commands), Problem Work Order Log (generated automatically with failure information at the time of failure; some input fields will allow the operator to input status and emergency notification information), Alarm Log (will contain information about warning and critical alarm events), Daily Diary Log (generated automatically when a user with Operator authority logs on to the system; some input fields in this log will allow the operator to input free form text information), Special Event Log (will contain information about scheduled special events), and System Operation Schedule Log (contains information about scheduled operations).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This section details the specific types of logs available for display and export by the Operator, fulfilling the 'Display system information logs' step of the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: At any point in an opening or closing sequence, the sequence shall be halted if: a device fails to report completion of the current sequence step within the response time window allotted for the step.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific trigger condition (timeout) for halting the sequence, representing an exception path.

evidence_cards.content: At any point in an opening or closing sequence, the sequence shall be halted if the status of a closure device, which was previously opened at the current entrance, changes to 'unknown' or 'closed', without an operator-initiated command.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific trigger condition (unauthorized state change during opening) for halting the sequence.

evidence_cards.content: At any point in an opening or closing sequence, the sequence shall be halted if the status of a closure device, which was previously closed at the current entrance, changes to 'unknown' or 'open', without an operator-initiated command.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific trigger condition (unauthorized state change during closing) for halting the sequence.

evidence_cards.content: At any point in an opening sequence, the sequence shall be halted if the status of a closure device for the opposite direction of travel changes to 'unknown' or 'open'.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a safety-related trigger condition involving the opposite direction of travel that interrupts the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: To resume an opening or closing sequence after a halt has occurred, the operator shall be able to issue a command to resume if the offending device status can be corrected within a configurable time period as defined in the database and in non-volatile memory.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the recovery behavior allowing the process to continue after the exception condition is resolved.
